title: Kickin Smoky Jamaican Dried Shrimp Curry
description: A flavorful and earthy Jamaican dish featuring dried shrimp, binchotan charcoal, and a blend of spices, perfect for a lazy Sunday, this satvik-friendly curry is a delight to the senses. It combines the snappy taste of dried shrimp with the richness of coconut milk and the depth of smoky binchotan charcoal.
instructions: Start by rehydrating the dried shrimp in water for about 30 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Light the binchotan charcoal and let it burn until it is covered in a thin layer of ash, then set aside to infuse the dish with smoky flavor.
In a large pan, heat some oil over medium heat and saute the chopped onion until it is translucent.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pan and cook for another minute, stirring constantly.
Add the curry powder to the pan and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the spices are fragrant.
Add the rehydrated dried shrimp, salt, and black pepper to the pan, and stir to combine.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and let the curry simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the flavors have melded together and the shrimp are fully coated.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed, adding more salt, pepper, or scotch bonnet peppers if desired.
Serve the curry hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.
